I am currently in a class for a DUI I received 3 years ago, at the height of my drinking. (I’m 3 months sober now). This past Tuesday I shared my story of sobriety and how God and Reimage Church were, and still are, my saving grace of sobriety. This is part of what I said to them “On Sunday July 20th of this year I started severely bleeding internally from damage I had done to my body by drinking heavily for years, and I had to have emergency surgery. I received prayers from dozens of people I didn’t even know from multiple prayer groups/churches, and believe those prayers and the grace of god saved me. The next day I started my sobriety journey. My doctors and family encouraged me to go to AA, but I had done that before and did not like the atmosphere. Instead I prayed about it. The next Sunday July 27th, I was compelled to pray with one of the leaders when the song “slow me down” was playing. I was greeted by Karen who listened to my prayer request and prayed with me. She has been someone Ive been thankful for since we met because it felt like she opened a doorway of hope into my life. Since that day my faith has grown stronger, I’ve met more people at church who still pray for me and check on me, and my sobriety has been reinforced by the strength I’ve gained through Reimage. I attribute my ability to stay sober and the healing of my body to God and the people I’ve met through Reimage.” I told the class more about my battle with alcohol before I mentioned God and my church saving my life and my future. But while I was sharing and after, I was thanked by some who may have been going down the same road I had been on and many people started open conversations about their experiences with faith. I believe it was a blessing to have been the one to start that conversation and to share how AA isn’t for everyone and maybe the best way to battle their demons is by putting God and church in their lives.
